name: sae_k32_time_layer_m1
what: TopK sparse autoencoder over residue-level BioEmu denoiser hidden states. This is the base SAE: the k=32, time-conditioned, layer -1 ablation arm.
why_this_one: It is the arm every downstream artifact binds to. configs/steering/abl1000u_cold.yaml, configs/steering/examples/train_rg_adapter.yaml and .../infer_rg_adapter.yaml all declare this checkpoint's SHA-256 as their `sae` source checkpoint, so it is the SAE that the shipped steering adapter models/rg_adapter_cold_v1.pt was trained against.

evaluation.note: Concept ranking uses cross-validated f1_per_domain with sequence-grouped folds. Coverage floors are 100 positive residues, 10 positive domain instances and 10 positive sequences.

provenance_notes: The bytes here are identical to outputs/ablations_interpro/k32_time_layer_m1/sae.pt as produced by the original run; only the location differs. Nothing in the fingerprinting machinery records a checkpoint PATH -- _source_hashes in bioemu/steering_workflow.py compares digests -- so shipping a copy at this path moves no fingerprint.

The training split in data/splits/ is the exact split this checkpoint was trained on. It is committed because re-deriving it does not reproduce it: the UniRef50 release is unpinned upstream and InterPro is queried live. See docs/DATA_PROVENANCE.md.

The absolute `evaluation_activation_archive` path in configs/ablations/k32_time_layer_m1.yaml is deliberately left as-is: that file's bytes are SHA-256'd into run identity and compared against stored provenance, so editing it would invalidate published artifacts.
caveats: Optimizer, scaler and scheduler states are removed for release; the weights are bit-identical to the trained checkpoint and the forward pass reproduces it exactly.
